newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends shade weaker on RBI dollar buying.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends shade weaker on RBI dollar buying.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed a fraction weaker at 35.7000/7050 against the dollar on Tuesday following central bank intervention to arrest the rupee's rise, dealers said.
The rupee started the day on a steady note at 35.6950/7025 per dollar, with early deals at 35.70.
The rupee had been expected to hold at this level on expectations that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) would continue to support the dollar through "passive intervention", dealers said.

The RBI has not been asking for quotes, but has been buying dollars from banks approaching it for over a week now. This is known "passive intervention", in contrast to the RBI's previous active intervention.
On Tuesday morning, the RBI surprised the market by turning away banks approaching it with dollars.
"Maybe they wanted to keep the surprise element and did not want the market to take them for granted," said a bank dealer.
In the absence of RBI demand and lack of demand from any other buyer, the rupee revived to 35.6900/50 per dollar.
The the RBI then hit the market, first directly, buying at rates up to 35.7050 and later passively, dealers said.
"He (the RBI) must have bought about $50-60 million today," said the chief dealer at a Bombay bank.
Forward premiums opened slightly firm in the morning but near months receiving pressure pulled down premiums by about one paise as the day progressed, dealers said.
The six-month annualised forward premium closed Tuesday at 3.70 percent compared to the previous close of 3.54 percent, largely reflecting a spurt in call money rates, dealers said.
